content.title: Is Starbucks open on Easter?
content.text: Key PointsStarbucks hours vary by store location.Customers should check the app or store locator for holiday hours.Starbucks reported 4% global sales growth and $9.9 billion in quarterly revenue. Just because it’s a holiday weekend doesn’t mean you can live without coffee. So if a Starbucks run is part of your Sunday routine, you may be wondering whether you can still grab that dirty chai latte or mocha this holiday. Starbucks does not enforce a company-wide holiday schedule, meaning individual stores set their own hours based on staffing, location, and demand. The short answer: Yes, most Starbucks locations are open on Easter. While many standalone cafés and drive-thru locations remain open, some locations, including those inside grocery stores, malls, or smaller communities, may have reduced hours or be closed for the day. Customers planning a coffee run should check ahead using the Starbucks app or online store locator to confirm local hours and avoid surprises. Easter is not typically considered one of Starbucks’ major closure holidays, unlike Thanksgiving or Christmas Day, when more widespread closures or reduced hours are common. For travelers, last-minute shoppers, or anyone hosting Easter brunch, odds are good the nearest Starbucks will be open. The Starbucks app will tell customers if their local Starbucks is open. Photo by BalkansCat on Getty Images Starbucks’ turnaround plan and recent earnings highlights Easter 2026 comes just after the end of Q1, as Starbucks is still in the early phase of its multi-year “Back to Starbucks” turnaround strategy under CEO Brian Niccol. Niccol has so far focused on improving customer experience, service speed, and store operations. The company has invested roughly $500 million into staffing, labor hours, and store improvements to support the turnaround, Reuters reported. Recent earnings show early progress, including about 4% global comparable sales growth and improving transaction trends, according to the company’s January earnings call. Quarterly revenue of about $9.9 billion, reflecting continued top-line growth 4% global comparable sales growth $9.9 billion in quarterly revenue U.S. transaction growth for first time in eight quarters Operating income of approximately $867 million (down from $1.2 billion) North America margin of about 11.9% (down from 16.7%) Effective tax rate of approximately 61.7%.
